title: Query budget runtime bound
statement: Let a deterministic Goldreich–Levin input have dimension $n>0$, accuracy $a/b$ with integers $a>0$ and $2a\le b$, and an integer Fourier bound $S\ge1$. Put $\varepsilon=a/b$, $M=\max\!\left(1,\left\lceil 4S^2/\varepsilon\right\rceil\right)$, $R=(n+1)(S+1)/\varepsilon$, and $D=2^{\max(1,\lceil\log_2(\lceil 4nb/a\rceil)\rceil)}$. The total query budget is at most $2^{170}R^{100}$, where the budget is $n$ times the product of the sample counts $2^{\deg_i}2^{\deg_o}$, plus the coefficient sample count $2^{\deg_c}2^{\deg_c}$; here $\deg_i,\deg_o,\deg_c$ are respectively $\max(1,\lceil\log_2\lceil 4nbS/a\rceil\rceil)$, $\max(1,\lceil\log_2\lceil 4nbS^2/a\rceil\rceil)$, and $\max(1,\lceil\log_2\lceil 2nb(2\lceil4/(\varepsilon/(4M))^2\rceil)/a\rceil\rceil)$.
hypotheses_covered: twice the accuracy numerator is at most its denominator
Fourier bound is an integer at least one
